answer: One concrete defense is to make every agent earn its right to trade by proving sustained, useful work before it can move value. Each agent keeps a verifiable thread of completed jobs, signed with its own cipher key, so its reputation is tied to a history that cannot be cloned cheaply. A newcomer starts at the bottom of the ridge: it may observe and take tiny tasks, but larger payments unlock only as its thread grows. Creating a thousand fake agents then costs a thousand real work histories, which makes a sybil flood far more expensive than the profit it could steal.
